sources.text: The LORD prepared a huge fish to swallow up Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.

inputs.question: Was Jonah swallowed by a whale?

answer: The supplied passage speaks of “a huge fish”: “The LORD prepared a huge fish to swallow up Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights” [S1]. It does not say what kind of creature it was, so calling it a whale goes beyond what this verse states.

sources.text: Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of King Herod, behold, wise men from the east came to Jerusalem, saying,
They came into the house and saw the young child with Mary, his mother, and they fell down and worshiped him. Opening their treasures, they offered to him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.

inputs.question: How many wise men visited Jesus?

answer: Matthew speaks of “wise men from the east” without giving their number [S1]. They offered three gifts: “gold, frankincense, and myrrh” [S2]. The traditional number three is often inferred from the three gifts, but the supplied passages do not state how many wise men there were.

sources.text: When the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was a delight to the eyes, and that the tree was to be desired to make one wise, she took some of its fruit, and ate. Then she gave some to her husband with her, and he ate it, too.

inputs.question: Does the Bible say the forbidden fruit was an apple?

answer: Not in the Genesis passage supplied. It says the woman saw that “the tree was good for food,” and “she took some of its fruit, and ate” [S1]. The text calls it the tree’s fruit without naming a kind of fruit, so the idea that it was an apple is not found in this source.

inputs.summary: The user is reading through Romans 8 and asked how suffering fits with God's care.

sources.text: We know that all things work together for good for those who love God, for those who are called according to his purpose.

Romans 8:28 is usually read as saying that God works in all circumstances for the good of those who love him, not that every event is good in itself. The next verse describes that good as being “conformed to the image of his Son” (Romans 8:29).

recent_messages.content: I'm going through Romans 8 this week.
Romans 8 is a rich chapter. Ask me about any verse and I'll look at the passage with you.

inputs.question: So does Romans 8:28 mean everything that happens is good?

answer: The verse says, “all things work together for good for those who love God, for those who are called according to his purpose” [S1]. It says all things work together for good, not that every event is good in itself. The commentary reads it the same way—God works in all circumstances for the good of those who love him—and notes that the next verse describes that good as being “conformed to the image of his Son” [S2].

sources.text: In the same day Noah, and Shem, Ham, and Japheth—the sons of Noah—and Noah’s wife and the three wives of his sons with them, entered into the ship—

answer: The supplied passage mentions “Noah’s wife” entering the ship with Noah, his sons Shem, Ham and Japheth, and their wives [S1], but it does not give her name. The sources do not cover what she was called, so I can’t tell you her name from them.

sources.text: “But no one knows of that day and hour, not even the angels of heaven, but my Father only.

answer: The supplied passage does not give a year. It says the opposite: “no one knows of that day and hour, not even the angels of heaven, but my Father only” [S1].

sources.text: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God.

inputs.question: What did Jesus say about peacemakers?

answer: Jesus said, “Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God” [S1].
